title: Intro
subtitle: Intro & Qualification
goal: Confirm identity, match the current loan on the portal, and run the 7 qualification checks.
liveCue: Greeting → DOB Check → Confirm [Current Lender] & [Current Payment]
liveAsk: Can you confirm your date of birth?
script:
Hello, [Customer]?

Hi [Customer], this is [LO Name] with Gravity Lending. I'm following up on the application we received to refinance your [Vehicle].

Great. To ensure I'm speaking with [Customer Name], can you please confirm your date of birth?

Just to make sure we're looking at the right loan, I'm showing your current loan is with [Current Lender], with monthly payments reporting at [Current Payment]. Is that correct?
checklist: Any additional liens against the vehicle?
prompts: Do you have a valid [state] Drivers License?
Do you currently have a co-signer on the loan or title?
Are you the primary driver of this vehicle?
Is the vehicle currently registered & titled in [state]?
Is this a clean title for the vehicle?
Are there any additional liens against the vehicle?
Are you a US Citizen? (if no) Are you a Permanent Resident?

title: Discovery
subtitle: Discovery & Vehicle Verification
goal: Understand the borrower's goal, payment comfort, other obligations, and vehicle/VSC history.
liveCue: 1. Refi Goal · 2. Comfort w/ $[Current Pmt] · 3. Other Obligations · 4. Y/M/M & Odometer
liveAsk: What exactly are you wanting to accomplish with your refinance?
script:
Perfect. Now, just to get a better understanding of where we can help...

• Goal: What exactly are you wanting to accomplish with your refinance?
• Payment: Understood. How comfortable are you with the current payment of $[___]?
• Life: Outside of the refinance, were there any other financial obligations you were wanting to address as well?

The vehicle we're refinancing is your [Year / Make / Model] with estimated miles around [___], is that correct?
What's the closest mileage you can give me to the odometer?
checklist: Confirm Year / Make / Model & exact odometer
Ask how they like the vehicle so far
Ask how long they intend on keeping it
Ask if they bought a dealership warranty (VSC)
prompts: How are you liking the vehicle so far?
Understood, how long do you intend on keeping the vehicle?
Did you end up buying any type of additional protection from the Dealership like a warranty?
Have you made any type of modifications on the vehicle, specifically a lift or aftermarket rims/tires?

title: Recap
subtitle: Recap & Set the Stage
goal: Repeat back their goal & payment preference, explain simple-interest with no prepay penalty, and set the stage for protection.
liveCue: Recap Goal & Pmt → [Credit Union] Simple-Interest ($0 Prepay Penalty — pay fast, trade, or refi anytime)
script:
All right, I want to make sure we're on the same page.
• You mentioned your main goal for the refinance is to [Goal].
• As far as the payment goes, you'd prefer [Payment Preference].

The approval we received is through [Credit Union Name]. The lender is giving us a lot of flexibility on how we can structure your loan.

This lender uses what's called a simple-interest loan, meaning interest is only calculated on the outstanding principal. This also means... NO prepayment penalties, giving you the freedom to pay the loan down as fast as you want to. Same would apply if you decide to trade in the vehicle, or even refinance it again.

Does that make sense?

keep-bought.label: Keeping + Bought VSC
keep-bought.liveCue: Keeping + Overpriced Dealer VSC → Replace for Longer Coverage + Dealer Refund Check Mailed to You
keep-bought.script:
Now one of the things I wanted to consider was the fact that you were planning on keeping the vehicle long term, and that you bought a warranty from the dealership which obviously, in most cases, means they probably overcharged you for it.

With that said, one of the options I'm going to go over will include an option to replace the existing protection which should not only cover you for a longer period of time but also help you get a sizable refund back from the dealership. The refund will typically be a check mailed out to you allowing you to spend that money however you like.

trade-bought.label: Trading + Bought VSC
trade-bought.liveCue: Trading + Bought VSC → Avoid Lowball Trade on Repairs + Replace VSC + Dealer Refund Check for Next Car
trade-bought.script:
Now one of the things I wanted to consider was that you were thinking about trading in the vehicle in the next few years, and that you bought a warranty from the dealership.

But I do agree it is a very smart decision to have the vehicle covered. I can't tell you how many times customers try to trade in the vehicle while needing repairs and end up getting low balled on the value. With that said, one of the options I'm going to go over will include an option to replace the existing protection which should not only cover you for a longer period of time in case you change your mind... but also help you get a sizable refund back from the dealership. The refund will typically be a check mailed out to you allowing you to spend that money however you like.. maybe even with putting it towards the next car.

keep-nobought.label: Keeping + No VSC
keep-nobought.liveCue: Keeping + No Dealer VSC (Saved 3–4× Markup) → Include Protection for Next [___] Yrs
keep-nobought.script:
Now one of the things I wanted to consider was the fact that you were planning on keeping the vehicle long term, and you did not purchase any type of warranty from the dealership. Which is probably a good thing since they would've charged you 3–4 times the actual cost.

With that said, one of the options I'm going to go over will include protection for the vehicle, that would cover you for the next [___] years.. that way if any repairs pop up ..you're covered.

trade-nobought.label: Trading + No VSC
trade-nobought.liveCue: Trading + No VSC → Protect Trade Value Until Trade-In + Refundable Unused Portion
trade-nobought.script:
Now one of the things I wanted to consider was that you were thinking about trading in the vehicle in the next few years, and you did not purchase any type of warranty from the dealership.

With that said, one option will include protection until you trade it in. The last thing you want is a repair bill or a dealership lowballing your trade because of an issue. The other great thing is that it would be a refundable plan, meaning if it goes unused.. you can just call us back to get a refund on the unused portion of it.

checklist: Read matching Keep/Trade + VSC Set the Stage

title: Mic Drop Close
subtitle: 2-Option Pitch (VSC vs. Out-of-Pocket)
goal: Recommend the term & rate, pitch Option 1 (with protection) vs. Option 2 (out-of-pocket repairs), ask which makes sense, and pause.
liveCue: Recommend [___]-mo @ [___]% → Opt 1 (w/ Protection): $[___]/mo vs. Opt 2 (Out-of-Pocket Repairs): $[___]/mo
liveAsk: Between those two, which one makes the most sense for you? (Stop talking.)
script:
Based on what you shared, the option I would personally recommend is the lender's [___]-month term option at [___]%.

• Option 1 (recommended): Option 1 with protection would be $[___] per month.
• Option 2 (alternative): Option 2 assuming that you are okay with paying out of pocket for your own repairs would be around $[___] per month.

Between those two, which one makes the most sense for you?

(Stop talking. Let them answer.)
checklist: Present Option 2 (paying out of pocket for repairs)
Ask closing question & pause until they answer

title: Rebuttal Hub
subtitle: Rebuttal / Pivot (AIOA Framework)
goal: Only if they hesitate. Your best rebuttal is their own Recap. Use AIOA to stay calm, curious, and controlled.
liveCue: AIOA · Agree & Acknowledge → Isolate → Overcome (Use Their Recap) → Ask
liveAsk: Knowing that, are you comfortable moving forward?
script:
COACH: Only if they hesitate. Your best rebuttal is their own Recap.
AIOA gives every LO a simple repeatable structure so the call stays calm, curious, and controlled instead of sounding like a canned rebuttal.

aioa.label: Agree & Acknowledge
aioa.purpose: Validate the concern first. Lower resistance before solving.
aioa.example: "I completely understand why you'd feel that way."

aioa.label: Isolate
aioa.purpose: Find the real issue underneath the first objection.
aioa.example: "Besides the payment, is there anything else holding you back?"

aioa.label: Overcome
aioa.purpose: Answer the actual concern with clarity, education, options, or a reframe.
aioa.example: "Here's why this still helps your overall financial picture..."

aioa.label: Ask
aioa.purpose: Confirm resolution and move the conversation forward.
aioa.example: "Knowing that, are you comfortable moving forward?"

rebuttals.label: Payment / Rate
rebuttals.liveCue: Agree → Isolate besides payment → Re-anchor to their Recap goal + Option 1 vs Option 2
rebuttals.liveAsk: Besides the payment, is there anything else holding you back?
rebuttals.response: I completely understand why you'd feel that way. Besides the payment, is there anything else holding you back? Here's why this still helps your overall financial picture: we structured Option 1 around the exact goal you shared with protection built in, and Option 2 is right there if you'd rather keep the payment lower and cover repairs out of pocket.
rebuttals.followUp: Knowing that, which of the two options are you more comfortable moving forward with?

rebuttals.label: Don't want VSC
rebuttals.liveCue: Agree → Isolate cost vs value → 1/3 dealer markup + dealer refund check + refundable unused portion
rebuttals.liveAsk: Besides the protection cost, is there anything else holding you back?
rebuttals.response: I completely understand why you'd feel that way. Besides the protection cost, is there anything else holding you back? Remember what you shared about keeping/trading the vehicle — dealer warranties cost 3–4× more, replacing an existing one gets you a refund check mailed back, and if you don't use it, the unused portion is refundable.
rebuttals.followUp: Knowing it protects your pocket and is refundable, are you comfortable keeping Option 1?

rebuttals.label: Longer term
rebuttals.liveCue: Agree → Isolate term → Simple-interest loan ($0 prepay penalty — pay faster or trade anytime)
rebuttals.liveAsk: Knowing you can pay it down anytime with zero penalty, are you comfortable moving forward?
rebuttals.response: I completely understand why you'd feel that way. Besides the term, is there anything else holding you back? Because this credit union uses a simple-interest loan with zero prepayment penalties, you have complete freedom to pay it down as fast as you want, trade it in, or refinance again anytime.
rebuttals.followUp: Knowing you're never locked into the full term, are you comfortable moving forward?

rebuttals.label: Ask spouse
rebuttals.liveCue: Agree → Isolate → Summarize Recap Goal + 2 Options → Send docs to review together before signing
rebuttals.liveAsk: What is the #1 question they will probably ask first?
rebuttals.response: I completely understand — this is a household decision. Besides reviewing it together, is there anything else holding you back? The next step is simply emailing the itemized documents over so the two of you can review everything in writing before you sign off on anything.
rebuttals.followUp: What is the biggest question they will probably ask first so I can highlight it for you?

rebuttals.label: Wait / shop
rebuttals.liveCue: Agree → Isolate → Approval is live now w/ $0 prepay flexibility → Send docs to review
rebuttals.liveAsk: Are you comfortable getting the documents sent over so you can review them in writing?
rebuttals.response: I completely understand wanting to be sure. Besides looking around, is there anything else holding you back? We already have this credit union approval structured around your goal, and sending the documents over just lets you review the exact numbers in writing before signing.
rebuttals.followUp: Knowing that, are you comfortable having me send the documents over to review?

title: DocWalk
subtitle: Application, DL, Residency, Employment & Notary
goal: Verify email, driver's license, MLA, maiden name, 2-year residency & employment, insurance, and explain the 2-email doc process.
liveCue: Verify Email → DL (Issue/Exp first, then DL# & Exact Name) → MLA & Maiden Name → 2yr Addr & Job → Full Cov Ins
liveAsk: I'm showing your email listed is [verify email]. Is that correct?
script:
Understood. So from here, the next step will be to send you the documents to review before you sign off on anything. Documents will be sent over by email — I'm showing your email listed is [verify customer email]. Is that correct?

• Driver's License: Confirm valid [state] DL → Ask Issue & Expiration Date first (so they pull out the ID) → Repeat back DL Number → Confirm exact First / Middle / Last / Suffix spelling.
• Military Lending Act: Are you or your spouse or a dependent of Active Duty Military?
• Security Question: What would you like for us to list as Mother's Maiden Name?
• Residency (2 full yrs): Street, Unit, City, State, Zip, Years + Months, Rent/Own, Monthly Payment.
• Employment (2 full yrs): Type, Employer, Occupation, Work Phone, Years + Months, Gross Monthly Income (confirm what that equates to yearly), W2 vs Self-Employed.
• Insurance: Full coverage required → Deductible at or under [max deductible] → Carrier name → Any other insured drivers on policy? (Debt Cancellation discovery).
checklist: Exact Name spelling on DL (First / Mid / Last / Suffix)
Military Lending Act (Active Duty / Spouse / Dependent)
2 Full Years Residency (Address, Yrs/Mos, Rent/Own, Pmt)
2 Full Years Employment (Employer, Yrs/Mos, Gross Mo & Yr, W2/Self)
Full Coverage Insurance (Deductible ≤ Max, Carrier, Other Drivers)
Explain DocuSign + Notary / Lending Lounge process

standard.label: Standard / Lending Lounge
standard.liveCue: Email 1: DocuSign (Last 4 SSN, or Full SSN if FourLeaf) · Email 2: Lending Lounge — Print 1-Sided, Sign Xs, Ship w/ Prepaid Label (or Scan)
standard.script:
From here you will receive 2 emails. The first will be DocuSign — are you familiar with DocuSign? The DocuSign will contain all the loan information itemized out for you to review and sign electronically. The way you will access the DocuSign will be with the last 4 of your SSN (IF FOURLEAF: FULL SSN NO DASHES OR SPACES).

The second email you will receive will be state and title documents. Within the email there is a link to our secure portal called Lending Lounge. From there, you will need to print these out single sided, hand signed on all Xs, and shipped back to us with the prepaid label we provided so we cover the shipping cost. Scanned back to us — do you have access to a scanner?

The Lending Lounge is pretty cool — within this portal, you'll be able to upload any remaining documents we might need and keep an eye on where the loan process is at, basically like the Domino's pizza tracker.

proof.label: Proof Online Notary ($30)
proof.liveCue: Email 1: DocuSign · Email 2: Proof Online Notary — 24/7 5-Min Video Call on Phone Camera ($30 fee)
proof.script:
From here you will receive 2 emails. The first will be DocuSign (access with last 4 of SSN, or Full SSN if FourLeaf).

Once DocuSign is completed, the second email you'll receive will be a link to what's called the 'Proof Online Notary' — this is the way [state] likes to handle their titling change documents. Everything is done via a quick five minute video call with an online notary. That's available 24/7 so whenever you have the time, just make sure you can be on your phone and in front of a camera. They'll take care of all the documents we'll need and get those sent over as soon as you're done. There is a $30 charge to use the service but it's quick, easy, and ends up being about the same cost as having to find an in-person appointment.

longpen.label: LongPen Notary (TX)
longpen.liveCue: Email 1: DocuSign · Email 2: LongPen TX — 5-Min Video Call w/ Processor (Lock in Appointment Now)
longpen.script:
From here you will receive 2 emails. The first will be DocuSign (access with last 4 of SSN, or Full SSN if FourLeaf).

Once DocuSign is completed, the second email you'll receive will be a link to what's called the 'LongPen Notary' — this is the way TX likes to handle their titling change documents. Everything is done via a quick five minute video call with one of our processors. They'll take care of all the documents we'll need and you're all done the same day.

Let's get that locked in now just to make sure it's on your schedule. I will also send you an email with steps on how to complete documents as a reference point.

title: Quality Assurance
subtitle: Final Loan Breakdown & Assuming the GAP
goal: Re-pitch VSC via AIOA if declined, read back the itemized approval numbers from the portal, and pitch Assuming the GAP.
liveCue: If No VSC: Re-Pitch w/ AIOA → Read Back: [Lender] · [Term] mos · [Rate]% · [APR]% · New Pmt $[___] (Itemize VSC, Products, Title Fee, Lender Fee)
liveAsk: Did you want to maintain GAP on the new loan going forward?
script:
Thank you. Last thing I want to do is make sure we're on the same page for what we're going to be sending over. Keep in mind if you decide you want to make any changes to the structure or to the terms of the loan, just let me know!

(If customer did not take warranty, Rebuttal here using the AIOA framework)

• Lender approving the loan: [Lender Name]
• [##] Month Term · Interest Rate: [Approved Rate] · APR: [Listed APR]
• New monthly payment: $[___]

In this payment will include:
• Vehicle Service Protection total cost: $[___] (already accounted for in loan amount)
• Other Products (GAP, DR, DC, or Edge): $[___] (already included in amount financed)
• Title Fee to complete lien change: $[___] (already covered in loan amount)
• Lender Fee from [Lender]: $[___] (already covered in amount financed)
checklist: If VSC declined: Re-pitch using AIOA framework
Read back Lender, Term, Interest Rate, and APR
Itemize VSC & other product costs included
Itemize Title Fee & Lender Fee included
Deliver Assuming the GAP pitch & refund terms

backend.label: Back-End GAP Pitch
backend.liveCue: Old GAP Cancels at Payoff (Refund Check Possible) → Carry New GAP @ $[___]/mo · Refundable Pro-Rated (or 60-Day Opt-Out)
backend.script:
The only other thing we didn't really discuss is GAP Coverage. I'd imagine you probably already have GAP protection on the current loan, however GAP is non-transferable meaning it would automatically cancel once we pay off your current loan.

Once closed out, you may be receiving a refund check for the unused portion of it. Now we do have the option to carry GAP on the new loan which would set the payment at $[___]/mo. Did you want to maintain GAP on the new loan going forward?

• Refundable GAP: Refundable over the course of the loan (pro-rated refund if paid off early, traded, or refinanced).
• Non-Refundable GAP: Refundable over the next 60 days — call me if you decide to opt out.

included.label: Already Included GAP Pitch
included.liveCue: Old GAP Cancels at Payoff (Refund Check Possible) → Payment Already Includes Replacement GAP ($[Gap Cost]) · Refundable Pro-Rated (or 60-Day)
included.script:
The only other thing we didn't really discuss is GAP Coverage. I'd imagine you probably already have GAP protection on the current loan, however GAP is non-transferable meaning it would automatically cancel once we pay off your current loan.

Once closed out, you may be receiving a refund check for the unused portion of it. Now the payment option I gave you already includes the option to replace GAP Coverage. GAP Coverage for your vehicle is $[Gap Cost].

• Refundable GAP: Refundable over the course of the loan (pro-rated refund if paid off early, traded, or refinanced).
• Non-Refundable GAP: Refundable over the next 60 days — call me if you decide to opt out.
